summary: Monomoy Point Light on South Monomoy Island: work began in 1823, the cast-iron tower dates from 1849, keepers' families served until 1923, and the site is now in the refuge, boat only.

lens.where: not stated in the sources read

access.note: Reached only by boat across Monomoy National Wildlife Refuge; grounds open, dwelling and tower closed.

Light signalled the Monomoy Life-Saving Station that a shipwrecked crew was there; four men from the schooner Effort taken off. The LSS narrative dates it 20 November 1883; a list of wrecks in the same report dates the Effort at Chatham Station to 26 November (source 13).

corrections.why: The nomination and LighthouseFriends date the cast-iron tower to 1849; the 1823 structure was not cast iron.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: LighthouseFriends gives 1 November 1823; the NRHP nomination says construction began in 1823 and the first flame appeared in 1828. Both are reported; neither is resolved.
The NRHP quotes Willoughby for a fourth-order lens in 1855 and the 1857 List for a refit in 1849; LighthouseFriends dates a Henry-Lepaute fourth-order lens to 1857. Reported as disagreement.
The Light-House Board report gives an estimate of not exceeding $2,000 for remodelling and renovation; LighthouseFriends gives $2,600 requested to rebuild. Both are reported.

LighthouseFriends dates the discontinuance of the light and the Pollock Rip light vessel to 16 February 1923; the Bulletin says the channel opened on 17 February and allowed one lighthouse to be discontinued without naming it.

The LSS annual report for 1884 gives 20 November 1883 in its narrative for the Monomoy station and 26 November 1883 in its list of wrecks for the Chatham Station entry for the schooner Effort. Both are reported in the story; neither is resolved.

notes_for_editor: (1) Most of the keeper anecdotes, the 1900 pistol incident, the 1904 interview, the 1914 ring, the Bearse ownership, the 1964-2016 history and the visiting arrangements come from LighthouseFriends alone; they are attributed to it in the text and nothing was checked in primary records. (2) Chronicling America searches found no contemporary report of the 1900 incident or of Smith's 1910 death: 'Monomoy' with 'Smith' in Massachusetts 1899-1911 returned only OCR noise, and 'Monomoy Point' with 'lighthouse' 1900-1923 returned no hits. (3) LSS 1884: the day in November is 20 in two of the three editions read (annualreportofop00unit p. 171; lifesavingservic10unitrich) and 26 in annualreportope04servgoog; the story gives late November. (4) 'Keeper Tuttle' in the 1884 LSS report is the Monomoy Life-Saving Station's keeper, not the light keeper; the roster has Asa L. Jones as the light's keeper 1875-1886. (5) Left out of the story: the Elsie M. Smith wreck of February 1902 (LSS annual report year ending 30 June 1902, p. 30; scan p. 34). The report places the stranding at Orleans Beach on 13 February, with two lives lost, not at Monomoy, and LighthouseFriends' account of the Smith daughters pulling a dead fisherman from the surf names no place. (6) Dwelling figure: the Board's report says the estimate is not more than $2,000; LighthouseFriends says $2,600 was requested. Both are in the text. (7) The Bulletin OCR garbles the car's distance and time ('9!' miles, '2~' hours) and the treads; the story gives only the 20-minute trip and the horse-and-cart comparison in words, and the 10-inch treads. (8) Anna M. Smith (roster, 1910) and Annie Smith (LighthouseFriends, a month in charge) are not confirmed as one person. (9) The roster has Edward E. Brewer and Edward Eveleth Brewer for one 1910-1911 span under two spellings; both lines are kept, with a note. (10) Henry M. 'Harry' Bailey has one archive record covering Monomoy (1916-1917) and Sandy Neck (1918-1921); the link is on the Sandy Neck record. (11) The register nomination's 'next to impossible' line is on PDF p. 22; the thematic group nomination appended to the same file (PDF pp. 61-63) supplies the boat-only and refuge statements. (12) The record's 'structures' entry (cast iron, 1823, 14 m) conflicts with both the nomination and LighthouseFriends; the corrections above propose the 1849 date and about 40 ft (12.2 m). (13) The 1922 Light List height figure in an earlier draft is not in the NRHP text and has been dropped. (14) The USLHS lighthouse roster shows 17 principal keepers and a 1924 custodian line; Douglas H. Shepherd's two lines carry the same note. (15) The LSS station 'Monomoy' (us-ma-monomoy-point-life-saving-station) is not researched here. No photographs were found or proposed. FACT-CHECK 2026-10-22: (a) 'Congress approved' is now 'the U.S. government approved', as LighthouseFriends words it; (b) Lewis's 1842 'ruined condition' is now footnoted to the nomination as quoting Snow (second-hand); (c) the 1842 inspector is no longer given a title, since the sources read do not give one; (d) the 1883 Effort date is given as 20 November with the 26 November list entry noted (source 13); (e) the Bulletin's Shepherd car figures are OCR'd as '9! miles' and '2~ hours'; the story uses only the 20-minute trip and the 'hours' comparison; (f) the 1899 dwelling text is on scan p. 89 (item 140) and the 1900 entry on scan p. 60; both were located by item number, and both were read on the scan.
